## TL;DR

First-load placeholders now use page-shaped blocks and counts tied to their layout constants, with a shared delayed/minimum display lifecycle and reduced-motion support. Mission Control and Stories use one realistic block/row. The loading shell and route now use a default-mode `page-fade` transition, so they overlap and cross-fade while each stays in the main pane’s normal flex flow. The route component retains the `main-route` class. The scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

The skeleton audit covers all routes in `LOADING_SKELETON_ROUTES` and the view-level skeletons. Mission Control’s real content is a dashboard composition, so its placeholder is a single dashboard block rather than a grid of tall cards. Stories is a vertical list, so its placeholder is one representative row. This avoids suggesting content density that will not appear after loading. Work and Inputs continue to use their six and three columns from the shared board constants; responsive column behavior follows the same breakpoint logic as those boards. The remaining kinds are compact representations of their data region, with counts tied to shared values where those layouts expose them.

Static page chrome stays visible while the data region loads. The shared `PageSkeleton` lifecycle owns the show delay and minimum visible duration, and cached data avoids replacing already-rendered content with a skeleton during background refresh. Reduced-motion styling and tests keep animation static for users who request less motion. Tests cover lifecycle timing, cached loading, each skeleton kind’s count, route coverage, and the representative dashboard and Stories shapes.

Review identified two related transition failures. The former `out-in` transition completed the shell fade before starting the route fade, and it also faded the page header away on fast loads when no skeleton was visible. A previous attempt to overlap the children positioned the leaving shell absolutely; review then found that its desktop insets produced a mobile geometry jump. This turn replaced that structure with a RouterView slot around a default-mode Transition. The slot renders either the loading shell or the route component as the Transition child, allowing Vue to overlap them during their 120 ms opacity transitions. The route component receives `main-route` at its root, preserving the `.main > :not(.spin)` flex-fill/scroll contract. The header and shell are grouped in the outgoing loading child, while normal route content is present as the incoming child.

The reported `page-height-layout.test.ts` assertion expected a direct `<RouterView class="main-route" />`. Because Vue Router's slot is needed for the transition to cross-fade, the test now verifies the slotted component has the `main-route` class. The loading test asserts the default-mode transition and explicitly rejects `mode="out-in"`. This keeps the layout guarantee tied to the component that Vue renders while making the transition behavior visible in tests. No CSS positioning or inset adjustments were needed.

| Route or view | Real content layout | Skeleton shape / audit result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Control `/` | One dashboard composition | One dashboard block; no wrapping card grid |
| Work `/work` | Six-column task board with responsive behavior | Six columns sourced from `WORK_BOARD_COLUMN_COUNT` |
| Inputs `/inputs` | Three input lanes | Three lanes sourced from `INPUT_BOARD_COLUMN_COUNT` |
| Client Board `/client-board` | Three project lanes | Same shared three-lane input-board shape |
| Stories `/stories` | Vertical story list | One representative row |
| Checks `/checks` | Plan controls and check-step table | Compact table-shaped loading region |
| Check Runs | Run-history table | Minimal representative table row |
| Agents `/agents` | Agent cards and detected-agent rows | One representative card or row for the loading region |
| Releases `/releases` | Release summary and distribution cards | One representative placeholder per unknown region |
| Deployments `/deployments` | Service groups and branch matrix | Service/matrix shape with shared matrix column sizing |
| Dev `/dev` | Configured target cards, two columns on desktop | Target placeholders match the two-column layout |
| Secrets `/secrets` | Environment key ledger | Compact table rows |
| Settings `/settings` | Field sections and aligned setting rows | Section count uses `GENERAL_FIELD_SECTIONS.length` |
| Repo Context `/repo` and detail routes | Document or detail content varies by route | Minimal row shell where a specific data shape is not available |

## Approaches tried

I removed the absolute-position overlap treatment instead of adjusting its mobile offsets. With `mode="out-in"`, Vue removes the outgoing child before inserting the incoming child, so the leaving shell no longer needs to be layered over a second flex child. The result uses a single transition and opacity only, with no out-of-flow geometry to keep synchronized across breakpoints.

## Challenges and blockers

The queued validation message traced the prior close-out failure to the page-height source assertion, not to a runtime layout regression. The two targeted test files pass, including the precise reported test. The scoped RepoOS check initially found no remote worker meeting its link probe, then waited in the serialized local fallback queue. Once that slot opened, the stale build was rebuilt; formatting, lint, build, CSS layers, theme contrast, hard-coded color scan, rendered contrast audit, all 369 changed-path test files (5,112 passed and one skipped), and UI smoke passed. No source or test failure remained. The loading-state shot capture limitation recorded by earlier review remains: captures that retain an active `aria-busy` loading state are rejected by the capture flow, so no new loading-state screenshots are claimed here.

## Key learnings

Vue Router’s slot API lets the app transition between a loading shell and the resolved route without adding a wrapper that would break the main-pane flex contract. Default transition mode allows both children to participate in a genuine cross-fade; preserving the route root class keeps the page pane filling and scrolling as before. Tests should assert the rendered route component’s class and the transition mode independently, so layout and motion requirements both stay explicit.
